title: CLCON/297/2022 of JANKI NEGI Vs R K SUDHANSHU

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Contempt Petition No. 297 of 2022
Smt. Janki Negi
........Petitioner
Versus

Mr. R.K. Sudhanshu and others
........Respondents
Present:-
Mr. M.C. Kandpal, Senior Advocate assisted by
Mr. Manish Bisht, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. J.S. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State.
Judgment
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 In this contempt petition, it has been brought to
the notice of this Court that the order dated 22.11.2021
passed in Contempt Petition No. 578 of 2018, Smt. Janki
Negi v. Mr. Ranbir Singh, Principal Secretary, Forest,
Uttarakhand and others ("the first contempt petition"), has
been wilfully disobeyed by the respondents. A response
affidavit has also been filed.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. It appears that initially the petitioner filed a writ
petition bearing WP (S/S) No. 36 of 2009, Smt. Janki Negi v.
State of Uttarakhand and others ("the petition") seeking

2
minimum wages and regularization of her services. The
petition was allowed by order dated 02.09.2016 and the
authorities were directed to consider the claim of the
petitioner for regularization, as also to pay minimum wages
to her till her services are regularized. The State aggrieved
by the order dated 02.09.2016 passed in the petition
challenged it in Special Appeal No. 398 of 2012, State of
Uttarakhand v. Smt. Janki Devi. The Special Appeal was
dismissed on 23.04.2018. The Division Bench of this Court
observed "We are unable to take a view contrary to what
was taken by learned Single Judge of this Court".
4. When the petitioner did not get the fruits of the
order dated 02.09.2016 passed by this Court in the petition,
she filed the first contempt petition. It was then brought to
the notice of this Court that, in fact, the services of the
petitioner have already been regularized, but she could not
get the entire money. The first contempt petition was
decided on 22.11.2021. The Court observed as hereunder:-
"6. Having regard to the fact that the service of
the petitioner has been regularized and the amount
of ` 1,38,168/- has been released to the petitioner,
therefore, in the humble opinion of this Court, the
order passed by Writ Court has been substantially
complied with.
7. Accordingly, contempt petition is closed.

3
8. Contempt notices issued to the respondent
nos. 1, 2 and 3 are hereby discharged.
9. However, petitioner shall be at liberty to
make representation to the Competent Authority
with regard to her claim for balance amount, if any,
as minimum of wages payable to her. If she makes
such representation within two weeks from today,
decision thereupon shall be taken within a period of
six weeks thereafter."
5. Subsequently, a representation was filed by the
petitioner, which has been rejected.
6. Learned Senior Counsel for the contempt petition
would submit that the petitioner has not been paid her
dues till her services were regularized.
7. Learned State Counsel would submit that the
representation has been decided by the respondent.
8. In fact, the question of regularization and
payment has already been considered by this Court in the
first contempt on 22.11.2021. The Court has then observed
that "the order passed by Writ Court has been
substantially complied with". In para 9 of the order dated
22.11.2021, passed in the first contempt petition, the Court
had given a liberty to the petitioner to make a
representation, which she did. But, it has been rejected.

4
9. The Court in its order dated 22.11.2021 passed
in the first contempt petition did not direct the respondent
to pay any amount to the petitioner. Direction for decision
on representation was given, which has been done.
Therefore, nothing survives in this contempt petition.
10. The contempt petition stands disposed of
accordingly. Notices issued to the respondents are hereby
discharged.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 16.05.2023
Avneet/
